key_insight: Calcite step defects enhance methane and ethane adsorption relative to flat regions, with methane showing higher excess adsorption than ethane.
engineering_relevance: Accounting for mineral surface defects can improve adsorption assessments relevant to oil and gas recovery from shale reservoirs.
method: MD simulations of methane and ethane near stepped calcite surfaces.
Restrained and unrestrained MD to isolate carbonate reorientation effects.
3D-RISM calculations on simulated structures and energy-minimized relaxed configurations.
evidence_signal: Both methods predict step-enhanced adsorption; 3D-RISM reproduces spatial patterns and overall trends at lower computational cost, but predicts lower peak densities and greater excess adsorption than MD.
watch_item: Use 3D-RISM for semi-quantitative screening rather than precise adsorption estimates because its peak densities and integrated excess adsorption differ from MD.
paper_title: Methane and ethane adsorption on calcite surfaces: effects of surface morphology from molecular dynamics and 3D-RISM
